newsitem.title: USA: CPUC approves higher Pacific Bell ISDN rate.
newsitem.headline: CPUC approves higher Pacific Bell ISDN rate.

text.p: The California Public Utilities Commission said Friday it approved increases in rates charged by Pacific Telesis Group's Pacific Bell unit for Integrated Services Digital Network services.
But the increases were lower than the company requested.
The regulatory body also directed Pacific Bell to improve ISDN customer service and to submit customer survey results for CPUC review over the next two years.

The commission's decision increased Pacific Bell's residential ISDN monthly rate by $5 to $29.50 from $24.50. The business rate will increase by $7.50 to $33.25 from $25.75. Pacific Bell had filed an application asking for an $8 increase for both business and residential customers.
The commission said it approved the increase because a product priced below market cost would discourage deployment.
ISDN technology is used to increase existing telephone line transmission capabilities. It makes possible simultaneous voice and data transfers over a single telephone line.

The commission also ordered Pacific Bell to offer residential customers 200 free hours of off-peak (evening) ISDN service per month. After 200 hours, customers will be charged the normal hourly usage fee. Pacific Bell had asked the commission to limit the number of free residential hours to 20 per month.

The commission said it found Pacific Bell's residential ISDN customer service to be inadequate. Representatives were hard to reach and poorly trained and customers requesting ISDN service were subjected to unreasonable delays, it said.

The commission ordered Pacific Bell to credit $25 to the customer's account for each ISDN service or installation appointment the company missed. The company will also discount its installation charge 10 percent for each day it fails to install ISDN service after 10 business days, it said.
The commission said it also ordered Pacific Bell to submit several customer surveys to the CPUC. The surveys will ask about customers' perceptions of the quality of service.
With the aim of encouraging resale competition, the commission ordered Pacific Bell to set wholesale rates for its ISDN service 17 percent below retail cost.
A Pacific Bell spokesman was not immediately available to comment.
